title: Angie Nixon Notches Another Win for the Left Through Old-Fashioned Organizing
partialText: State Representative Angie Nixon scored a stunning upset on Tuesday in Florida’s Democratic Senate primary. Her victory will test the strength of a democratic socialist in a red state.

title: A Stunning Win for the Left in Florida: 6 Takeaways From Tuesday’s Primaries
partialText: State Representative Angie Nixon, a progressive firebrand, defeated a moderate who dramatically out-raised her with grass-roots enthusiasm. Can it carry her to victory in November?

title: Mary Peltola and Dan Sullivan Advance in Key Alaska Senate Contest
partialText: Both parties see Alaska as key to winning the Senate. The state’s nonpartisan primary put Mary Peltola, a Democratic former congresswoman, on the same ballot as Dan Sullivan, the incumbent Republican she hopes to unseat. Both advanced to the general election.

title: ‘I’m Not That Informed on National Security,’ Graham Says in South Carolina Debate
partialText: Senator Darline Graham made the remark in a debate against Representative Ralph Norman, her opponent in the runoff election to succeed her brother, Lindsey Graham. Here are five takeaways from the debate.

partialText: Plus, the political emails are coming for you.

title: Trump, With Limited Options in Iran, Tries Economic Pressure — Again
partialText: Iran has survived decades of sanctions. Faced with more, it is likely to escalate rather than surrender, analysts said.

partialText: The Emirates has long been a major trading hub for Iran, and analysts say it has been key to Iranian efforts to evade international sanctions, which Emirati officials deny.

title: Israel Opens Criminal Investigation Into Killings of Hind Rajab and Gaza Medical Workers
partialText: Two high-profile cases that had spurred international condemnation of the country’s conduct in Gaza were transferred to the military police. Such investigations have rarely led to convictions.

title: How the Iran War Made Africa’s Richest Man Even Richer
partialText: Africans have turned to one of their own for fuel as the world’s supplies run low. But they are not the only ones with the continent’s richest man on speed dial.

title: How One County Profited From Data Centers Amid a Growing National Backlash
partialText: Loudoun County, Va., has gotten rich hosting more than 250 data centers, allowing it to cut property taxes. Other locales are taking note, even as a nationwide backlash over data centers grows.

title: Voters Aren’t Waiting for November to Try Ousting Officials Over Data Centers
partialText: As a backlash grows over data centers, more local officials are facing recall elections for their support of the computing sites.
